subject: SRA

options: raise the alarm and ensure people are evacuated safely
try to fight a large fire alone
explanation: Only use an extinguisher on small fires if trained and safe.

subject: SRA
body: If you find a suspicious package, you should
options: not touch it, clear the area and report it immediately
explanation: Use radios at a safe distance, as per site procedure.

subject: SRA
body: When taking a bomb threat call, you should
options: keep the caller talking and note every detail
tell the caller you are recording
explanation: Note the caller's voice, background noise and exact words.

subject: SRA

options: the assembly point using the safest route
explanation: Never use lifts in a fire.

subject: SRA
body: Patrols should be
options: at the same time every night
explanation: Predictable patrols are easy to avoid.

subject: SRA
body: Access control means
options: checking that only authorised people enter an area
explanation: Check ID and record visitors.

subject: SRA
body: At shift handover, guards should
options: brief the next guard and update the logbook
explanation: Continuity keeps the site secure.

subject: SRA
body: A good incident report answers
options: who, what, when, where, why and how
explanation: Keep it factual, clear and complete.

subject: SRA
body: Notes in a security logbook should be
options: accurate, factual and made at the time
explanation: They may be used as evidence.

subject: SRA
body: If a crime has taken place, the guard should
options: protect the scene and keep people out until police arrive
move evidence to a safe place
explanation: Preserve evidence.

subject: SRA
body: When dealing with an angry visitor, a guard should
options: stay calm, listen and use a respectful tone
explanation: De-escalation reduces risk.

subject: SRA
body: A professional guard should
options: share site information on social media
wear the correct uniform and licence and stay alert on duty
use their phone for long periods
explanation: Professional conduct builds trust.

subject: SRA
body: Information about the site and clients must be kept
explanation: Guards often see sensitive information.

subject: SRA
body: If a child is reported missing in a mall, the guard should
options: tell the parent to search alone
follow the lost child procedure and alert colleagues immediately
explanation: Act quickly and cover exits.

subject: SRA
body: A CCTV operator should
options: monitor screens, record incidents and alert patrolling guards
explanation: Footage may be evidence and must be handled carefully.

options: call for help and start CPR

subject: SRA

options: enough to search anyone by force

explanation: Call the police for arrests and investigations.

subject: SRA
body: When searching bags with consent, a guard should
options: follow site policy and ask the person to open the bag themselves
explanation: Always be respectful.

subject: SRA
body: Keys and access cards held by security should be
options: left in the guard room unlocked
signed in and out in a key register
explanation: This keeps them traceable.

subject: SRA
body: Before starting a patrol, a guard should
options: check equipment such as the radio and torch
explanation: Know the site layout and hazards.

subject: SRA

subject: SRA
body: When using a two-way radio, you should
options: think before speaking, keep messages short and clear
explanation: Clear radio use saves time in emergencies.

subject: SRA
body: Guards should not accept
options: gifts or bribes from visitors or contractors
explanation: This protects their integrity.

subject: SRA

subject: SRA
body: Corrections in a logbook should be made by
options: drawing a single line through the error and initialling it
explanation: The original entry must stay readable.

subject: SRA
body: To protect evidence at a crime scene, a guard should
options: not touch or move anything and note who enters
explanation: Police need the scene untouched.

subject: SRA
body: When a person with a disability needs help evacuating, guards should
options: follow the personal evacuation plan and assist them safely
ask them to wait until last without help
explanation: Refuge points and evacuation chairs may be available.

subject: SRA
body: A guard who sees a wet floor in a public area should
options: put up a warning sign and report it for cleaning
explanation: Prevent slips, trips and falls.
